items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: And Rosengarden was always recording someplace, he was always twenty minutes late, and Haggart didn’t want to be there in the first place, and Tony Mottola and Bucky, all of those guys, they rotated the schedule unto themselves

ctx.x: Clinics. He was suddenly discovering that world. And Rosengarden was always recording someplace, he was always twenty minutes late, and Haggart didn’t want to be there in the first place, and Tony Mottola and Bucky, all of those guys, they rotated the schedule unto themselves, but half the time they’d forget who was there. But it was probably the best, in my opinion, of this period. If you’re going to say — well it was probably the best organization. And it was their organization. Nobody talked. If you talked to…

God forbid, played arpeggios all the time. And we finished this tune and there was silence in 6B, and it was like a Kafka movie where all the — well I think it was thirty seconds, but all this time Mottola took a cloth and cleaned off first his guitar and then put it on the rack and slowly turned around and looked at him. That’s all he did. And we knew it was over, he was gone the next night. But I had many adventures like that. Many. I had Al Klink in that band, who came from the Miller band. He was the, when…

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I do some pop dates once in a while with Skitch Henderson.

ctx.x: I mean it. That was one of the most thrilling records I ever made with those guys. And then I’ve got some — I do some pop dates once in a while with Skitch Henderson. I do some with Palm Beach Pops. I’m going to do something in Syracuse this summer.
Right. With the symphony, that’s right.

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: So if somebody came on and Skitch would go into something, we never rehearsed.

ctx.x: Do you remember any funny or weird instance of The Tonight Show orchestra with people coming on that you had to back up?

Well you know that show was great, the band was great because we had everybody played whatever they felt when they were asked to do it. So if somebody came on and Skitch would go into something, we never rehearsed. Skitch never rehearsed. We had music up there and the only time we’d play is when they were off the air, we played for the audience and then you might hear a little of the band. But we were forever just getting there on time from another session just in time to play the theme.
No kidding. What a life, huh? You recorded some marvelous duo records, in fact I think you said some of your best things are duos?
